label: The lane brief encodes nine repair rules: structure-only edits; anchors from the matching template with numbered duplicate ids; missing docs reconstructed from spec.md plus git history with a dated note and Not recorded sentinels; broken links re-pointed or de-linked; generic single-word phrases replaced with folder-slug phrases; scaffold continuity placeholders filled; status aligned to spec.md; level set from the docs' own declarations; template headers added.

The long tail ran as 43 parallel lane briefs, each validating its own folder list and re-running repair-derived.cjs --apply after edits; lanes were told never to hand-edit graph-metadata.json or description.json.

Phase 013 states the safety properties as requirements: every scripted fix idempotent with a dry run before apply (NFR-R01); full corpus passes or each exception is listed (SC-001); reconstructed docs open with a dated note; archived packets keep their status with only structure and metadata changing.

Archive policy tension, recorded with both sources: upgrade-legacy.mjs says archived snapshots are only ever recorded, never rewritten (--include-archive opts in deliberately), and heal-spec-docs.cjs hard-skips z_archive/z_future; phase 013 cleaned and repaired archived packets. Reconciliation: snapshot immutability protects meaning, while validation repair changes only structure/metadata/paths, which the never-change-meaning rule permits.

The reconciliation both sources support: snapshot immutability is about what a document says; an archive-safe heal is legitimate when structural-only and explicitly opted in, but the contract is unstated today and reads as contradictory to an external user.

Two lane classes have no tool support at all: reconstructing a missing document from spec.md plus git history, and re-pointing broken links by finding the file's current path. Both are mechanical but currently lane work.

Phase 013's risk table names the control that makes mass structural repair defensible: scripts change only marker lines, fields and paths; lanes are told structure only; diffs are sampled. An external-user heal path must reproduce this evidence standard in its docs and tests.

direction: Treating the lane briefs as throwaway one-offs
reason: The brief is a coherent nine-rule specification with proven safety properties, and most rules map onto idempotent transformations a tool can own.

direction: Reading archive protection as an absolute prohibition on archive repair
reason: The pipeline's own --include-archive opt-in and phase 013's completed archive repair show the intended line is prose preservation, not structural immutability.
